questions.prompt: What was MIT's original location before moving to Cambridge in 1916?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Back Bay. Copley Square area. They moved in 1916. Some say crossing the Charles was the best decision they ever made.
questions.npcReactionWrong: MIT wasn't always in Cambridge. Before they crossed the river, they were in Back Bay.

questions.prompt: Harvard University was founded in what year, making it the oldest institution of higher education in the United States?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: 1636. Before the English Civil War. Before the Bill of Rights. Before everything. We've had time to cultivate our... reputation.
questions.npcReactionWrong: 1636. Harvard predates the country by over a century. Think about that.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the statue in Harvard Yard that tourists rub for luck, and what's ironic about it?
choices: John Adams statue - it's actually John Quincy Adams
Charles Eliot statue - students call it bad luck
John Harvard statue - 'Statue of Three Lies' (wrong date, wrong face, wrong title)
Samuel Adams statue - he never attended Harvard
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Wrong date of founding, the model wasn't actually John Harvard, and Harvard wasn't the founder—just an early benefactor. But people keep rubbing that shoe.
questions.npcReactionWrong: The John Harvard statue. Three lies: wrong date, wrong person as model, wrong title. He wasn't the founder.

questions.prompt: What famous artificial intelligence laboratory was founded at MIT in 1959?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: The AI Lab. McCarthy. Minsky. They thought machines could think. Turns out they were right. Eventually.
questions.npcReactionWrong: MIT helped invent the future. In 1959, they started the AI Lab. Changed computing forever.

questions.prompt: Cambridge was originally called what before being renamed after the English university?
questions.npcReactionCorrect: Newtowne. Renamed in 1638 to honor Cambridge University. Colonial ambition. Name a town after a school, hope some prestige rubs off.
questions.npcReactionWrong: Newtowne. Before they named this place Cambridge, flattering the English, it had another name.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What color is Harvard's official school color?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Crimson. Even children know that. The Harvard Crimson. The color of old money.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Crimson. Even children know Harvard's color. Do you?

alternateQuestions.prompt: What is the name of the Harvard/MIT bridge that measures length in 'Smoots'?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Harvard Bridge. The Smoot is named after Oliver Smoot, who was used as a measuring stick by his fraternity. The bridge is 364.4 Smoots plus or minus one ear.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Harvard Bridge. They measured it using a student named Smoot. MIT humor.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What MIT tradition involves placing unusual objects on the Great Dome?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: Hacks. They've put a police car up there. R2-D2. A phone booth. Engineering as art. Or mischief. Same thing at MIT.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: MIT hacks. Students put things where they don't belong. Police cars, fictional robots. It's tradition.

alternateQuestions.prompt: What Cambridge-based software, developed by Dan Bricklin and Bob Frankston, introduced the first spreadsheet?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: VisiCalc. Before Excel, before Lotus, there was VisiCalc. Changed business forever. Invented here.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: VisiCalc. The first spreadsheet. Developed here in Cambridge. Every accountant owes them.

alternateQuestions.prompt: Harvard Square is a hub of what public transit system?
alternateQuestions.npcReactionCorrect: The Red Line. If you take the T to Harvard Square, you're on the Red Line. Simple geography.
alternateQuestions.npcReactionWrong: Red Line. From Alewife through Cambridge to Boston. Harvard Square is one of the main stops.

redemptionChallenge.instructions: Match the discovery, invention, or person with the correct institution (Harvard or MIT). Get 6 of 8 correct.
redemptionChallenge.npcPassResponse: Acceptable. Not impressive. Acceptable. Sully would have gotten them all wrong, but he would have argued about it for an hour. Miss that.
redemptionChallenge.npcFailResponse: Four wrong. Out of eight. Do you know the acceptance rate at either of these institutions? You wouldn't make the waitlist.
